rationale: Private # methods were marked public and had to be pinned. The pre-ruling contract had them 'strip to clean names (field_definition already did)'. SUPERSEDED by the M49 W15 #813 ruling (owner: 'the symbol keeps the declared name'): the method is named `#secret` and carries visibility private. The forbidSymbols entry is inverted accordingly — `secret` (stripped) is now the WRONG name, because a reading edge that targets `#secret` could not resolve to a symbol named `secret`, and a class may legitimately declare both `x` and `#x` as distinct members.
